_shape: core/interiors.ts InteriorBlueprint — an architectural floor plan, not a node. It has no populations, no mapAsset and no adjacency: ecology lives on the town. Colour, style, materials and decoration are deliberately absent; this is the footprint the art lane paints to. Every physical feature below is traced to a shipped line in _featureSource, and every gap is named in _canonSilent rather than filled with a guess.
name: Hearthollow Inn
_room: 13 cells wide by 8 cells tall including the walls, so 11 by 6 of open floor. One plan cell is exactly one movement tile. Wide and shallow. The doorway is cut into the SOUTH wall, seventh cell from the west corner; the player walks in heading north and lands on the floor cell directly inside it.

_legend.#: SOLID — the player cannot walk through it. Every solid cell here is a wall: the outside walls of the common room, and the EAST wall, which is the partition between this room and the byre. The fire is in the WEST wall, at the end where Aldis stands. Note that the plan cannot distinguish a wall from a fixture; in this room there are no fixtures, so every solid cell is a wall.
Open floor of the common room. Nothing stands on it.
_legend.D: The doorway out to the green. This is the threshold cell; stepping onto it takes the player back to the town. There is exactly one, per the map-prompt rule that every building has one clearly visible door.
_legend.@: A named person stands here — Aldis, the innkeeper. The collision parser treats this cell as walkable floor; it is occupied in fact, and the scene layer stands her on it.
_legend.S: The tile the player stands on to take a room for the night. It faces north, directly at Aldis. There is no counter: the service is transacted with the person.

door._note: PINNED TO THE MAP'S OWN DOOR ANCHOR — no longer provisional. tools/mapgen/layouts/hearthollow.txt is the one document the painting and the collision mask are both stamped from, and it draws a 'D' door-anchor cell for every building — legend kind door-anchor, 'the walkable cell a building is entered from' — with its header naming which building each belongs to: 'inn (9,18)-(16,23) 8x6 = 128x96 door (13,24) long and low', and 'Every door is on the building's SOUTH face and every one of them is the end of a lane.' Cell (13,24) spans native (208..224, 384..400); x/y below are its CENTRE, so OverworldScene.doorTileOf — floor(x * balance.map.mapRenderScale / balance.map.tileStepPx) — lands on tile 13,24: the cell the layout marks, walkable in the shipped mask, with the inn's footprint blocked directly north of it. THIS REPLACES A PROVISIONAL COORDINATE, 296,392 = tile 18,24, that this note always said 'must be re-pinned against the painted map' and never was: it stood five tiles east of the inn on the open lane, with no building on any side. The owner played the deployed build and reported that none of the doors work; the trigger tile was not on the building he walked up to. tests/unit/doorway-threshold.test.ts holds every shipped door to this against the shipped mask. Units are map-native pixels in the 1024-square painted town, the same space data/nodes/hearthollow.json props use.

anchors._purpose: Aldis, the innkeeper, stands at the west end of the common room by the fire. Her own line puts the fire and the kettle at her end: 'Boots are by the fire, they were wringing wet, and the kettle's on.' She is the only person in this room.

The tile the player stands on to trigger the rest service — the full heal that costs inn ticks. It faces north, directly at Aldis. Deliberately no counter between them: the canon gives this inn no counter, desk, register or key hook, and one would be invented furniture.

_featureSource: THE BUILDING — tools/comfy/manifest.json _nodes.hearthollow.feature lists 'a long low inn with a byre' among the town's five buildings, sourced there to innkeeper-hearthollow.rest. docs/CAST-AND-VOICE.md on Aldis: she 'runs the only beds in a farming town', so this is the town's ONE inn. || THE FIRE, WITH FLOOR SPACE IN FRONT OF IT — innkeeper-hearthollow.rest, when {} (unconditional base state), verbatim: 'Boots are by the fire, they were wringing wet, and the kettle's on. Don't start thanking me for either.' Wet boots stand ON THE FLOOR at the fire, so the fire is at floor level in a wall with room to stand before it, and it is where Aldis is. Drawn into the WEST wall because that is the end away from the byre. || THE BYRE, AND THE SHUT DOOR TO IT — innkeeper-hearthollow.rest, when {}, verbatim: 'Your animals are in the byre with the door shut and that was done an hour since.' The byre is CITED as adjacent to this room and the door between them is CITED as shut. It is therefore drawn as the solid east partition, and the byre is not part of this floor plan. See _canonSilent. || ROOMS AND SUPPER SOLD FROM THIS ROOM — innkeeper-hearthollow.rest, when {}, verbatim: 'A night here is half a season gone, so sleep out and keep the days if you're wanted before the turn. Room only, or supper as well?' || ONE DOOR — tools/comfy/manifest.json map-town skeleton, the only sentence in the project that legislates doors: 'every building has one clearly visible door'. docs/build-doc.md's town-map class variant adds 'clear building entrances'. Neither places the door. || A DOOR IS MEANT TO BE USED — docs/content-bible.md's SFX set budgets 'door' and 'footsteps (grass, wood, stone)'. This is the closest the canon comes to sanctioning an interior; it sanctions the sound of a door and a wooden floor underfoot, and nothing more. || ALDIS — data/dialogue.json speaker innkeeper-hearthollow: name 'Aldis', portrait npc-innkeeper, home 'hearthollow'. Her entire shipped corpus is the two lines of innkeeper-hearthollow.rest quoted above.
_canonSilent: WHERE THIS BUILDING STANDS. The manifest places Hearthollow's five buildings 'well apart around one open grazing green' and gives no compass direction, no coordinate and no prop for the inn. Neither town has a prop for its inn or its shop: the only coordinates that exist in Hearthollow are 512,648 for the survey board. The door x/y above is no longer provisional: it is pinned to the door anchor tools/mapgen/layouts/hearthollow.txt draws for the INN, which is the same document the painting and the mask are stamped from. The dialogue canon still names no coordinate; the LAYOUT does, and it names the building too.

WHETHER THE PLAYER MAY ENTER THE BYRE. Aldis says the byre door is SHUT, which is the only thing established about it. The east partition is drawn solid and the byre is out of this plan. Whether it becomes a second room is the owner's call, not a gap to fill by guessing.

WHETHER BEDS APPEAR ON SCREEN. Aldis 'runs the only beds' in town, so beds exist as a fact of the business, but nothing anywhere describes a bed as a visible object, counts them, or places one. Nothing is drawn.
WHERE THE GUEST ROOMS ARE. 'Room only, or supper as well' is singular and transactional. Nothing says whether the rooms are on this floor, above it, or behind it, and nothing says how many there are.

WHETHER THERE IS A KITCHEN, A BACK ROOM, A STAIR, OR THE INNKEEPER'S OWN QUARTERS. Supper is served and a kettle is on the fire in the room the player stands in; no kitchen is named. Every stair in the whole dialogue corpus is in Bowerdeep — Pell's eastern stair, the floor stair the elder came up, and the one innkeeper-bowerdeep.rest hangs a key at. Importing one here would be cross-town invention.

WHETHER THERE IS A COUNTER, DESK, REGISTER OR KEY HOOK. No shop counter, desk or bar is described anywhere in the shipped content: every occurrence of the letters 'counter' under data/ is inside the word 'encounter'. The only key hook in the corpus is Bowerdeep's — innkeeper-bowerdeep.rest, 'The key's on the hook at the stair'. None is drawn, which is why the rest anchor faces the person and not a fixture.

HOW THE COMMON ROOM IS FURNISHED. Beds, tables, chairs, benches, a blanket press, a chimney: none is established for this building. The canon gives a fire with floor space before it and supper being served.

THE ROOM'S SIZE. The only size rule in the canon is exterior and relative — nothing standing on the ground may be wider than the lane is wide. 13 by 8 cells is an engineering choice made to fit the cited features, not a sourced dimension.

WHETHER THE INN HAS WINDOWS, AND WHAT ANY INTERIOR SURFACE IS MADE OF. The manifest declares Hearthollow's roof pitches and wall materials to be art choices in its 'concrete structure' class, explicitly not named content — the same is true inside. None of the four buildings in this set has a window in canon.
